title: Human iEEG 30-50 Hz exponent followed a GABA-A PET map in two pre-registered clips (55-56 patients), but mesial temporal channels carried most of the link and a second GABA-A map did not repeat it
abstract: Question: does the aperiodic exponent (chi) of human cortical field potentials, a proposed marker of excitation:inhibition (E:I) balance, follow regional GABA-A and glutamate receptor density? Data: OpenNeuro ds004100 (HUP iEEG, CC0), two 300-s interictal clips; 2,540 and 2,586 bipolar cortical channels outside seizure-onset and resected tissue in 55 and 56 patients; neuromaps PET maps (flumazenil GABA-A, Norgaard 2021, primary; NMDA; mGluR5; GABA-A alpha5; a second flumazenil map). Method: 30-50 Hz log-log slope; patient fixed effects; patient-cluster bootstrap; 1,000-rotation spin tests; plan hashed before analysis, clip 2 as replication. Results: chi rose with GABA-A density in both clips (+0.144 and +0.137 per SD; CIs +0.07 to +0.21; p_spin 0.002). An E:I index (GABA-A minus glutamate) and a T1w/T2w-adjusted model also passed. Other exponent fits agreed. NMDA and mGluR5 maps alone gave no relation. But the second flumazenil map gave no relation (+0.006, +0.018), and the alpha5 map gave the opposite sign. Post hoc, the link was only in inferior channels; superior channels gave -0.06 and -0.03. The 10% of channels with the lowest GABA-A density, mostly mesial inferior temporal, carried most of it: without them the slope was +0.04 (p_spin 0.12-0.16). Spatial-trend, seizure-onset-distance and T1w/T2w-thickness controls did not remove the full-sample slope. Conclusion: the pre-registered prediction passed, but the data do not show a cortex-wide receptor-graded E:I rule; a mesial temporal contrast explains most of the link. Limitations: epilepsy patients; same patients in both clips; template positions; map-dependent result; post hoc localisation.

display.caption: A: pre-registered slopes of the 30-50 Hz exponent per SD of GABA-A density, E:I index and GABA-A with a T1w/T2w covariate (blue run-01, orange run-02; grey = 95% spin-null range). B: per-patient Spearman correlations. C: patient-centred exponent in deciles of GABA-A density; the lowest decile carries most of the link.

Post hoc checks: spatial-trend, seizure-onset-distance, T1w/T2w-thickness and other-map controls keep the slope; removal of the lowest-density decile reduces it to about +0.04; the slope is in inferior (mostly medial) channels, not superior channels.

A: slopes for each receptor and control map in both clips; only maps built from the Norgaard GABA-A map pass with the predicted sign; the Dukart flumazenil map gives no relation and GABA-A alpha5 the opposite sign. B: other spectral outcomes agree.
